NumPy 2.5.4 is a development-only oracle. The JSON files include SHA-256
hashes of the exact pinned source files used to choose criteria. Regenerate
with generate.py and the fixed oracle environment. NumPy's license is retained
in NUMPY-LICENSE.txt. No NumPy runtime kernel is included in this module.

linalg.json:
  numpy/linalg/tests/test_linalg.py:67-73 (assert_almost_equal helper),
  143-157 (exact real/complex 2x2 inputs),
  487-503 (SolveCases residual), 581-587 (InvCases identity residual),
  974-986 (DetCases eigenvalue-product comparison).
  The source uses decimal=6 for float32/complex64 and decimal=12 for
  float64/complex128. numpy/testing/_private/utils.py assert_array_almost_equal
  uses an absolute difference below 1.5 * 10**(-decimal), separately for real
  and imaginary components. The test uses the stricter 10**(-decimal).
  Solve/inverse check the same residual, not an unapproved output tolerance.
  Determinants compare with the fixed oracle's double-component eigenvalue
  product, as in DetCases.

fft_identity.json:
  numpy/fft/tests/test_pocketfft.py:35-52,
  TestFFT1D.test_identity_long_short.
  Bounded random real/complex inputs of length 16, n=1..31, float32/float64
  components, backward normalization. Source criterion is rtol=0 and
  atol=5*spacing(array(1.,dtype)); tests apply that bound to round-trip results.
  Seed fixes inputs while preserving the original input range and conditions.
  Stored forward results support inspection; they are not used to claim that
  the round-trip criterion also approves forward-output comparisons.

fft_adaptation.json:
  Shape/dtype oracle only. Integer, boolean, float16, float32/64 and complex
  inputs, axis 0/-1, n=5, all normalizations. Numerical acceptance for these
  input/operation/dtype combinations remains pending; no tolerance invented.

Other numerical tests use exact small identities for shape, conjugation,
normalization, empty/singular cases, and execution/resource behavior. These
are regression tests, not full-family numerical acceptance.

Pending: direct transform output criteria beyond source-matched tests;
large/ill-conditioned/extreme-scale/non-finite inputs; broader linalg mixed
operand numerical criteria; platform acceptance; complete API families.
